transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really distressing memories and nightmares about a traumatic event that happened to me about a year ago. These memories just force their way into my mind out of nowhere, and I can't seem to stop them. It has gotten to the point where I really need some help.

Since this event happened a year ago, have you been experiencing persistent avoidance of things that remind you of the event, or have you noticed significant changes in your mood or how you react to your surroundings?

Yes, for the past year I've done everything I can to avoid thinking about it and stay away from any places or reminders of what happened. My mood has completely changed too, as I feel totally emotionally numb and disconnected from everyone. I also find myself constantly on edge, always scanning my surroundings for danger and unable to relax.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports symptoms including intrusive memories, nightmares, avoidance behavior, negative alterations in mood/cognition, and hyperarousal that have persisted for one year. This duration exceeds the one-month requirement for Acute Stress Disorder and does not fit the criteria for Adjustment Disorder, which is typically used when criteria for other specific disorders are not met. Therefore, the list has been narrowed to Posttraumatic Stress Disorder.
